questions.text: Which word has a long O sound, like in 'bone'?
questions.explanation: 'Home' has the long O sound. The silent E at the end makes the O say its name.

questions.text: Which word has a short E sound, like in 'bed'?
questions.explanation: 'Bend' has the short E sound. The other words all contain vowel teams that make a long E sound.

questions.text: The letters 'ea' in the word 'beach' make a long E sound. Which other word uses the 'ea' vowel team to make the same long E sound?
questions.explanation: 'Steal' uses the 'ea' vowel team to make the long E sound, just like 'beach.'

questions.text: What does the prefix 'un-' mean in the word 'unhappy'?
questions.explanation: The prefix 'un-' means 'not,' so 'unhappy' means 'not happy.'

questions.text: What does the suffix '-less' mean in the word 'careless'?
questions.explanation: The suffix '-less' means 'without,' so 'careless' means 'without care.'

questions.passage: Maya woke up early on Saturday morning. She packed a lunch, put on her boots, and headed to the trail with her dad. They hiked for two hours and spotted a deer near the stream.
questions.text: When did Maya and her dad go hiking?
questions.explanation: The passage states that Maya woke up early on Saturday morning before the hike.

questions.passage: Ben wanted to enter the science fair, but he did not know what to study. He noticed his plant wilting, and that gave him an idea. He decided to test whether plants grew better in sunlight or shade. He worked on it every day after school until the fair.
questions.text: How did Ben respond to not knowing what to study for the science fair?
options: He gave up and did not enter.
He asked his teacher to pick a topic.
He got an idea from observing his plant and got to work.
questions.explanation: Ben noticed his wilting plant, got an idea for an experiment, and worked on it every day — showing he solved his problem by paying attention and taking action.

questions.passage: The rain went pitter-patter on the roof. It drip-drip-dripped down the window.
questions.text: What effect do the words 'pitter-patter' and 'drip-drip-dripped' have in this passage?
options: They show the narrator is angry.
They make the reader feel sad.
They copy the sound of rain and create rhythm.
They describe the color of the rain.
questions.explanation: 'Pitter-patter' and 'drip-drip-dripped' are sound words that imitate the noise of rain and give the passage a rhythmic, musical quality.

questions.passage: When Cora first got her puppy, Max, he hid under the bed all day. Slowly, Cora tempted him out with treats and gentle pets. A week later, Max raced around the yard, tail wagging, ready to play.
questions.text: Which event happens at the BEGINNING of this story?
options: Max wags his tail while playing.
Max hides under the bed all day.
Cora gives Max treats and pets.
questions.explanation: The beginning of the story introduces Max hiding under the bed, before Cora coaxes him out and he becomes comfortable.

questions.passage: "I love the snow!" said Priya. "We can build a snowman!" "I wish the sun would come back," said her brother Raj. "My hands are already freezing."
questions.text: How are Priya's and Raj's points of view about snow different?
options: Priya is afraid of snow; Raj is not.
Priya is excited about the snow; Raj does not like the cold.
Both Priya and Raj love the snow.
Both Priya and Raj want to go inside.
questions.explanation: Priya is excited and wants to build a snowman, while Raj is uncomfortable and wishes the sun would come back — they have opposite feelings about the snow.

questions.passage: The monarch butterfly travels up to 3,000 miles each year. It flies south to Mexico in the fall and returns north in the spring. Scientists are still learning how monarchs find their way.
questions.text: Where do monarch butterflies travel in the fall?
questions.explanation: The text says monarch butterflies fly south to Mexico in the fall.

questions.passage: First, a caterpillar hatches from an egg. Then it eats leaves and grows larger. Next, it forms a chrysalis. Finally, it emerges as a butterfly.
questions.text: What happens right AFTER the caterpillar forms a chrysalis?
questions.explanation: According to the passage, the caterpillar forms a chrysalis and then finally emerges as a butterfly — that step comes right after.

questions.passage: Volcanoes can erupt and release hot melted rock called lava. Lava flows slowly down the side of the volcano.
questions.text: Based on the passage, what is lava?
options: Hot melted rock released by a volcano
questions.explanation: The text directly explains that lava is the hot melted rock released when a volcano erupts.

questions.passage: This book explains why washing your hands is the best way to stop the spread of germs. It describes the correct way to scrub, rinse, and dry your hands.
questions.text: What is the main purpose of this book?
options: To tell a funny story about soap
To describe different types of germs
To explain how and why to wash your hands properly
To persuade readers to buy a new soap brand
questions.explanation: The author's main purpose is to explain why hand-washing matters and to describe the correct way to do it.

questions.text: Which sentence uses the correct past tense of the verb 'run'?
questions.explanation: 'Ran' is the correct irregular past tense of 'run.' Adding '-ed' or '-ned' is incorrect because 'run' is an irregular verb.

questions.text: Which sentence is written with correct capitalization?
questions.explanation: Both 'Thanksgiving' (a holiday) and 'November' (a proper name for a month) must be capitalized.

questions.passage: The trail was so narrow that we had to walk in a single-file line. There was barely enough room for one person at a time.
questions.text: Based on the sentences, what does the word 'narrow' mean?
questions.explanation: The context clue 'barely enough room for one person' shows that 'narrow' means not wide, or thin.

questions.text: The word 'preview' starts with the prefix 'pre-.' Based on the meaning of 'pre-' (before), what does 'preview' most likely mean?
options: To watch something for the very first time ever
To see something before it is officially shown
questions.explanation: The prefix 'pre-' means 'before,' so a 'preview' is a chance to see something before it is officially released or shown.
